title: Daily Standup Checklist
metaDescription: A daily standup checklist to keep your agile team's daily meeting short, focused, and useful: the three questions, blockers, and next steps. Free, or tailor it with AI in Gisti.
cardDesc: Keep the daily standup short and useful — the three questions, blockers, and clear next steps.
intro: The daily standup should take 15 minutes and leave the team clearer, not drained. It slides into a status report or a problem-solving session the moment it loses discipline. This checklist keeps it tight and genuinely useful. Use it as-is, or open it in Gisti to adapt it to your team, and see the rest of our work and onboarding checklists.

items.note: A visible timer keeps everyone honest.

items.text: Same time, same place (or link), every working day
Everyone stands or stays on camera to keep it brief
Each person shares what they did yesterday
Each person shares what they're doing today

items.note: The blockers are the real point of the meeting — surface them clearly.

items.text: Update the board or tracker before or during standup so it reflects reality
Flag blockers clearly and name who can help unblock them
Take detailed discussions offline: "let's take that after standup"
items.note: A quick parking lot keeps two people from stalling the whole team.

items.text: Note action items and their owners
Keep the focus on progress toward the sprint or team goal
Don't let it become a status report aimed at the manager
items.note: Standup is for the team to coordinate with each other, not to report upward.

items.text: Rotate or assign a facilitator to keep time and flow
Follow up on yesterday's blockers to make sure they got resolved
End with clear next steps and who's doing what

faq.q: What are the three questions in a daily standup?
faq.a: Each team member answers: what did I do yesterday, what am I doing today, and are there any blockers in my way? The first two keep the team aware of progress, and the third — blockers — is the most important, because it's where the team can actually help each other move faster.

faq.q: How long should a daily standup be?
faq.a: Fifteen minutes or less. It's meant to be a quick sync, not a working session. If a topic needs deeper discussion, note it and take it offline with just the people involved right after standup, so the rest of the team isn't held hostage to a two-person conversation.

faq.q: How do I make standups more effective?
faq.a: Keep it timeboxed and at the same time each day, have everyone update the board beforehand, and focus on blockers and coordination rather than status reporting to a manager. Move detailed problem-solving to a parking lot after the meeting, rotate the facilitator, and always follow up on yesterday's blockers so they don't linger.
